## Ready to practise? {#readiness}

Solve $4(x-2)-3(x+1)=2x-5$ **on paper**, then select your answer.

<div class="index-check" role="group" aria-label="Choose the solution of the linear equation">

<button type="button" data-choice="a" aria-pressed="false">A. $x=0$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="b" aria-pressed="false">B. $x=-16$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="c" aria-pressed="false">C. $x=-6$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="d" aria-pressed="false">D. $x=6$</button>

</div>

<div class="check-feedback" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
<div data-result="a" hidden>

**Check the constant from the subtracted bracket.** In $-3(x+1)$, multiply both terms by $-3$: the constant is $-3$, not $+3$. Correct that expansion and try again.

</div>
<div data-result="b" hidden>

**Check how you remove a subtracted constant.** If you reach $-11=x-5$, add $5$ to both sides. Subtracting another $5$ does not isolate $x$. Try again.

</div>
<div data-result="c" hidden>

**Correct.** Expand, simplify and use equal operations on both sides.

$\begin{aligned}
4x-8-3x-3&=2x-5\\
x-11&=2x-5\\
-x-11&=-5\\
-x&=6\\
x&=-6
\end{aligned}$

**Check:** $\text{LHS}=4(-8)-3(-5)=-17$; $\text{RHS}=2(-6)-5=-17$.

</div>
<div data-result="d" hidden>

**Check the negative coefficient.** Subtracting $2x$ from $x$ gives $-x$. From $-x=6$, divide both sides by $-1$. Try again.

</div>
</div>

<button class="reset-check" type="button" hidden>Try again from the start</button>
